prompt_name: Implement FastPrep Compare Against Standard V4
prompt:
You are working inside an existing Python/Tkinter repository called Train Type Data Preparation Tool. Do not rewrite the application from scratch. Do not invent new architecture. Modify the existing files and add only the missing pieces required below. If something is ambiguous, inspect the repo first and then implement the smallest safe change.

CURRENT REPO CONTEXT
- Entry point: main.py
- Config: app/config.py
- Runtime asset copy: app/runtime_assets.py
- Existing comparison package: app/comparison/
  - models.py
  - workbook_comparator.py
  - report_generator.py
- Existing UI for comparison: app/ui/compare_tab.py
- Existing generator is separate and must not be broken: app/services/rebuild.py
- Existing comparison currently does cell-by-cell value comparison and produces a report with columns: Change No, Change Type, Sheet Name, Cell Address, Standard Value, Project Value.

MAIN GOAL
Implement Compare Against Standard V4. The user should choose only a Project FastPrep .xlsm workbook. The application should automatically use an embedded standard FastPrep workbook from data/standards/7_7_2/. It must compare the standard workbook against the project workbook and generate a new Excel report file named Workbook_Deviations.xlsx. The output report must contain this exact column order:
1. Change No
2. Sheet
3. Cell
4. Standard Value
5. Project Value
6. Parameter
7. Rule

IMPORTANT OUTPUT FORMAT
- Generate .xlsx, not .xls. openpyxl writes .xlsx reliably.
- Do not modify or save either source .xlsm file.
- Standard workbook and project workbook must be read-only inputs.
- The only output is the report workbook.

STANDARD WORKBOOK TO EMBED
Place this file in the repo:
data/standards/7_7_2/standard_7_7_2_precalculated_UNLOCKED.xlsm

Also create:
data/standards/7_7_2/standard_metadata.json

Use this metadata content as the starting point, adjusting only if the exact workbook filename differs:
{
  "standard_id": "fastprep_7_7_2_generic",
  "display_name": "FastPrep 7.7.2 Generic Standard",
  "baseline": "7.7.2",
  "train_type": "Generic",
  "workbook_file": "standard_7_7_2_precalculated_UNLOCKED.xlsm",
  "read_only": true,
  "precalculated": true,
  "password": "IDDP_Protection_842",
  "compare": {
    "mode": "visible_minus_blacklist",
    "report_name": "Workbook_Deviations.xlsx",
    "report_sheet_name": "List of Project Deviations",
    "ignored_sheets": [
      "Cockpit",

    ],

      "Default_"
    ]
  },
  "passive_rules": {
    "enabled": true,
    "sheet_name": "Passive Rules Check",
    "header_row": 182,
    "data_start_row": 183,
    "columns": {
      "rule": "A",
      "position": "B",
      "parameter": "C",
      "quantity": "D",
      "sheet": "E",

      "column_offset": "G",
      "regular_next_offset": "H",
      "next_row_offset": "I",
      "next_column_offset": "J",
      "find_after": "K",

    }
  },
  "report_columns": [

  ],
  "user_warning": "Before comparison, open the project FastPrep workbook in Excel, enable macros/content, recalculate, save, and then run comparison."
}

WHY THIS METADATA EXISTS
- It identifies which standard workbook the app should use.
- It gives the UI a display name.
- It keeps ignored sheets and Passive Rules settings out of hardcoded Python code.
- It allows future support for additional standards like 7_8_0 without rewriting the comparator.

KNOWN FACTS FROM ANALYSIS OF A REAL PROJECT WORKBOOK
Use these facts to guide implementation, but do not hardcode row data except where explicitly stated:
- Real project workbook example has 81 sheets: 54 visible and 27 veryHidden.
- Workbook has VBA, no external links, no connections.
- Workbook calculation mode is manual.
- Passive Rules Check exists and is visible in the project workbook.
- Passive Rules Check header row is row 182.
- Passive Rules Check data start row is row 183.
- Passive Rules Check headers in row 182 are: Rule, Pos, parameter, Qty, sheet, Roffset, Coffset, Regularnextoffset, NextRoffset, NextCoffset, findafter, Name for display, Value for Display, Rule Check, Rule explanation.
- Passive Rules contains about 1113 parameter navigation rows, about 176 rules, and about 473 unique parameters in the sample workbook.
- Passive Rules references many sheets, including Train type, Dynamic train data set, Communication config., Project, Fixed train data set, INAT Train type STM, Test Binary Inputs, Test Binary Outputs, Development, IMU, COMET, ATC2, Hardware plug, and others. Therefore, do not exclude all Test* sheets by default. Some project deviations are located in Test* sheets.
- Cockpit contains a manual deviations list starting around row 96 in the sample workbook, but Cockpit must remain ignored for cell comparison because it is a presentation/status sheet, not a source data sheet.

SHEET SELECTION RULES
Implement sheet selection from metadata:
- Compare only visible sheets by default.
- Exclude any sheet in compare.ignored_sheets.
- Exclude any sheet whose name starts with any prefix in compare.ignored_prefixes.
- Do not exclude Test* sheets globally. Test sheets can contain real project deviations.
- Do not compare veryHidden sheets by default.

Recommended ignored sheets for V4 are:
- Cockpit
- Revision history
- Design Deviations from STD
- Verify_Import_XML
- Passive Rules Check
- REF
- XML_Reader
- CustomerData
- Fixed_Parameters
- Default_Parameters
- any sheet starting with Default_

Do not hardcode only this list in workbook_comparator.py. Load it from standard_metadata.json.

PASSIVE RULES ENRICHMENT
Add a new module:
app/comparison/passive_rules_parser.py

Implement a PassiveRulesParser that builds a mapping from (sheet_name, cell_address) to one or more matches containing parameter and rule.

Data source:
- Use the STANDARD workbook, not the project workbook, to build the map.
- Load the standard workbook read-only with data_only=True.
- Read Passive Rules Check according to metadata settings.

Parsing algorithm:
1. Read the Passive Rules Check sheet.
2. Start at data_start_row from metadata, default row 183.
3. Track the current rule. If column A has a non-empty value, it becomes the current rule. If column A is empty, reuse the previous rule.
4. For each row, read:
   - parameter from column C
   - sheet from column E
   - Roffset from column F
   - Coffset from column G
   - findafter from column K
   - display_name from column L
5. Skip rows without parameter or sheet.
6. If the referenced sheet does not exist in the standard workbook, skip the row safely.
7. Locate the parameter in the referenced sheet:
   - If findafter is present, first locate a cell whose normalized value equals findafter. Then search for the parameter after that anchor in row-major order.
   - If findafter is not present, search the whole referenced sheet for a cell whose normalized string value equals the parameter.
   - Exact match after stripping whitespace. Do not use fuzzy matching.
8. Once the parameter anchor cell is found, compute target cell:
   - target row = anchor row + int(Roffset)
   - target column = anchor column + int(Coffset)
9. Map (sheet, target_cell_address) to PassiveRuleMatch(parameter, rule).
10. If display_name is available, use display_name as Parameter in the report. Otherwise use parameter.
11. If multiple Passive Rules map to the same cell, join distinct parameter names with "; " and distinct rule IDs with "; ".
12. If no rule maps to a changed cell, leave Parameter and Rule empty in the report.

Important: make this parser fault-tolerant. Bad rows in Passive Rules must not crash the comparison. Log warnings and continue.

MODELS
Modify app/comparison/models.py. Keep backward compatibility as much as possible. Extend DeviationRecord to include parameter and rule:
@dataclass(slots=True)
class DeviationRecord:
    change_type: str
    sheet_name: str
    cell_address: str
    standard_value: Any
    project_value: Any
    parameter: str = ""
    rule: str = ""

Do not remove change_type internally yet, because existing comparator logic and tests may rely on it. The report does not have to display change_type.

WORKBOOK LOADING
In WorkbookComparator:
- Load both workbooks with openpyxl.load_workbook(..., data_only=True, read_only=True, keep_vba=True).
- If standard workbook or project workbook is encrypted/password-protected, keep existing msoffcrypto fallback.
- Do not call save() on either source workbook.
- Continue closing workbooks after comparison.

FORMULA / RECALCULATION WARNING
Because FastPrep uses manual calculation mode and many formulas, the app must warn users in the UI:
Before comparison, open the Project FastPrep workbook in Excel, enable macros/content, recalculate the workbook, save it, and then run comparison.
The Python code must not attempt to recalculate Excel formulas or run macros.

COMPARISON LOGIC
Update WorkbookComparator:
- Accept optional metadata object or metadata path.
- Load standard_metadata.json for ignored sheets, ignored prefixes, report settings, passive rules settings.
- Build passive_map once after loading the standard workbook.
- For each changed cell, get passive match by (sheet_name, cell_address).
- Add parameter and rule to DeviationRecord.
- Keep missing sheet handling. For missing sheets, set Cell to "-", Parameter and Rule empty. Since the output report has no Change Type column, use:
  - Standard Value = "Exists" and Project Value = "Missing" for missing project sheet
  - Standard Value = "Missing" and Project Value = "Exists" for project-only sheet

VALUE NORMALIZATION
Keep comparison deterministic:
- Treat None and blank/whitespace-only strings as None.
- Trim string values.
- Normalize CRLF to LF for strings.
- Do not convert numeric-looking strings to numbers. Leading zero strings like "00000004" must remain strings.
- Do not compare formatting, colors, formulas, comments, row heights, column widths, VBA, or metadata. Compare values only.

REPORT GENERATION
Modify app/comparison/report_generator.py. The report worksheet must be named "List of Project Deviations". Headers must be exactly:
Change No, Sheet, Cell, Standard Value, Project Value, Parameter, Rule

Write each deviation sorted by (sheet_name, cell_address). Do not include Change Type in the report columns. Use clean formatting:
- Dark blue header background
- White bold header text
- Freeze panes at A2
- Auto filter on used range
- Reasonable widths: Change No 12, Sheet 28, Cell 12, Standard Value 28, Project Value 28, Parameter 32, Rule 22
- Wrap text for Standard Value and Project Value

UI CHANGES
Modify app/ui/compare_tab.py:
- The user should only browse for Project Workbook.
- Standard Workbook should be loaded automatically from metadata/config.
- Show the selected standard display name, e.g. "FastPrep 7.7.2 Generic Standard".
- Add the warning text about recalculation.
- Preview columns must match the final report: Sheet, Cell, Standard Value, Project Value, Parameter, Rule.
- Keep the current preview-before-save workflow.
- Continue asking the user where to save Workbook_Deviations.xlsx.

CONFIG AND RUNTIME ASSETS
Modify app/config.py:
- Add DATA_STANDARDS_DIR, STANDARD_7_7_2_DIR, STANDARD_7_7_2_WORKBOOK, STANDARD_7_7_2_METADATA_FILE.
- Add matching RESOURCE_* paths for bundled data.

Modify app/runtime_assets.py:
- Ensure data/standards/7_7_2 exists.
- Copy bundled standard workbook and standard_metadata.json to runtime data if missing.

PyInstaller/build:
- If build.ps1 already bundles data;data, this should be enough if the standard is under data/. Verify this. Do not add a new top-level folder unless necessary.

TESTS
Add or update tests. If no tests folder exists, create one. At minimum test:
1. ReportGenerator writes headers exactly:
   Change No, Sheet, Cell, Standard Value, Project Value, Parameter, Rule
2. DeviationRecord supports parameter and rule fields.
3. WorkbookComparator still detects a changed cell and missing sheets.
4. PassiveRulesParser can parse a tiny synthetic workbook with a Passive Rules Check sheet and map a changed cell to Parameter and Rule.
5. UI changes should not be unit-tested unless existing UI tests exist.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
The work is done only when all criteria are true:
- App starts successfully.
- Generate Train Type tab still works.
- Compare Workbook tab no longer requires user to select a standard workbook.
- Compare Workbook tab automatically uses data/standards/7_7_2/standard_7_7_2_precalculated_UNLOCKED.xlsm.
- User selects only a project .xlsm.
- App compares standard vs project without modifying either workbook.
- Report file is created as .xlsx.
- Report sheet is named "List of Project Deviations".
- Report columns are exactly: Change No, Sheet, Cell, Standard Value, Project Value, Parameter, Rule.
- For cells mapped by Passive Rules, Parameter and Rule are filled.
- For cells not mapped by Passive Rules, Parameter and Rule are blank.
- No hardcoded absolute paths.
- No internet/network calls.
- No macro execution.
- No source workbook saving.

DO NOT DO THESE THINGS
- Do not rewrite the whole app.
- Do not remove the existing Train Type generator.
- Do not compare XML files in this version. XML comparison is for a future version.
- Do not rely on pandas. Use openpyxl and existing msoffcrypto fallback.
- Do not use fuzzy matching for parameters.
- Do not invent sheets or rules that are not in the workbook.
- Do not hardcode project-specific deviations from Cockpit into the generated report. The report must come from actual workbook comparison.
- Do not modify or save FastPrep .xlsm source workbooks.

IMPLEMENTATION ORDER
1. Add standard metadata and config paths.
2. Update runtime asset copy.
3. Extend DeviationRecord.
4. Update ReportGenerator to V4 columns.
5. Update WorkbookComparator to read metadata and automatic standard settings.
6. Add PassiveRulesParser.
7. Enrich deviations with Parameter and Rule.
8. Update CompareTab UI to auto-standard and V4 preview columns.
9. Add/update tests.
10. Run tests and fix failures without changing requested behavior.
